articleTitle: Cyber-Physical Co-Simulation Testbed for Real-Time Reactive Power Control in Smart Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Existing electric power distribution systems are evolving and changing as a result of the high renewable energy sources integration. Hence, future smart distribution networks will involve various technical challenges; one of them is real-time monitoring and controlling the network to operate it effectively and efficiently. This paper develops and analyzes a cyber-physical co-simulation testbed for real-time reactive power control in the smart distribution network. The testbed is a two-layer system, with Typhoon HIL 604 representing the physical layer and the other layer as a cybernetic layer. The cybernetic layer is used to model a test system and control reactive power from smart inverters in real-time. The implementation of real-time reactive power control of smart inverters on a CIGRE MV distribution network is shown in this study. The proposed testbed's usefulness in real-time reactive power control is demonstrated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimal Strategy for Customer Directrix Load based Demand Response Considering Comfort and Preference of Customers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Demand response (DR) plays an important role in promoting the accommodation of renewable energy (RE) and easing the regulation burden of power systems. This paper proposes an optimal strategy for customer directrix load (CDL) based DR that takes into account customer comfort and preference. First, CDLs are formulated based on the RE profiles and nodal loads as well as network constraints, which are released to customers as the targets to unlock their flexibility. Moreover, the regulating capacity of customers is characterized based on the typical weekly load by downsampling methods. Finally, an optimal decision model is developed considering comfort and preference of power consumption, where customers are enabled to participate in DR, whilst maintaining their comfort. The validity of the proposed strategy is corroborated through simulation tests and the results indicate the accommodation of RE is significantly enhanced.

articleTitle: A Novel Preventive Frequency Stability Constrained OPF Considering Wind Power Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel preventive frequency stability constrained optimal power flow analysis in a power system model with a wind farm. As for the frequency stability analysis, the loss of the total wind power output is simulated considering the most severe wind output fluctuation scenario. Primary frequency response of the system after the wind power output loss is investigated by time-domain simulation approach. As the frequency stability constraint, the system frequency deviation after the wind output variation is constrained within a permissible range. In IEEE 39-bus system, the relationships between the capacities of the wind farm and the frequency deviations are analyzed. The influence of the frequency stability constraint on generator scheduling results is discussed.

articleTitle: Investigating Demand-Side Management (DSM) Opportunities Using Load Profiling: The Case of Qatar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: High penetration of renewable energy is fundamental to the sustainable development of the electricity grid. It offers great environmental, economic, and social benefits. However, due to the intermittent nature of renewable energy resources, maintaining the supply-demand balance will be a key challenge. Demand-Side Management (DSM) is a prominent solution. Identifying the best DSM policy to adopt is not an easy task. Thus, awareness of consumer behavior and smart grid applications is necessary. This may be achieved through load profiling and load clustering. In this paper, we analyze residential consumer behavior in Qatar using unpublished smart meter data to understand the relationship between electricity usage and weather patterns and to be able to differentiate between paying and non-paying customers. Our study uses a sample size of 20 customers, 10 paying and 10 non-paying. First, the recent advances in load profiling and load clustering are reviewed. Then, we identify the residential demand trends in Qatar. The study also investigates the challenges of applying DSM techniques in the region and suggests policy recommendations. Additionally, we discuss possible future research directions in load profiling and load clustering.

articleTitle: Three-Phase SRF PLL Model for System Frequency Response Studies in Low-Inertia Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper derives a small-signal model of a three-phase synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop for use in system frequency response studies assuming a system of balanced three-phase voltages. The small-signal model is described by a second-order transfer function which relates the actual to the estimated grid frequency. The small-signal model behaves identically to the large-signal model for small disturbances. Simulation results demonstrate that phase-locked loop dynamics can be neglected in the high-inertia scenarios, while in the low-inertia scenarios they have a significant impact on the grid frequency and should be included in models.

articleTitle: Distance protection of inverter based renewables power evacuating lines and downstream network: Issues and mitigation approach
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Inverter based renewables (IBR) can adversely influence the reliability of distance relay which is the most ubiquitous form of protection for long high voltage transmission is endangered. Especially, distance protection of lines which are connected directly at the point of connection (POC) of the IBR are more prone to failures. In this paper, we extend a more generic discussion on issues with distance relays by including relays which are even downstream to the POC. This analysis is important from the perspective of reliable operation of a coordinated system of distance relays. The paper also presents a mitigation approach which can potentially enhance relay effectiveness without requiring any new information or infra-structural changes to the traditional implementation. The proposed solution can be implemented as a modification of the existing algorithms. We use numerical simulations of a modified IEEE 39 bus test system to analyze and demonstrate.

articleTitle: Transformation of Existing Commercial Building Cluster Towards Renewable Rich Microgrid: A Case Study for Marina Bay Sands Singapore
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Existing commercial-building-clusters in Singapore commonly draw entire electrical power from the fossil-fuel based utility grid. In this paper, a case study of potential sustainability efforts at Marina Bay Sands (MBS) building-cluster is presented to demonstrate the feasibility and benefits of its transformation towards a renewable rich microgrid. A careful investigation shows that a hybrid AC/DC microgrid installation with solar energy and battery energy storage sized to 5 % and 10% respectively of the average daily energy demand is feasible, considering the economic and space constraints. It is also analysed that installation cost benefits amounting to S$ 51,000/MWh can be obtained from optimal sizing of battery energy storage, net cost savings of S$ 26,000/MWh can be obtained due to low labour charges for proposed floating solar PV installation, whereas average net daily cost savings upto S$ 41,540 can be obtained through strategic demand response measures at MBS. Simulation results for the proposed microgrid design is also presented to show stable and satisfactory 24 hour microgrid operation for various solar energy penetrations and load demand scenarios.

articleTitle: Suggestions on Improving the Carbon Spot Market and Developing China's Carbon Futures Market
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In carbon market, futures are essential products to help market participants to discover price and manage market risk. This article analyzed the futures in European Union Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS) and Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) and summarized the experience of carbon futures trading. However, the spot market of China's national ETS is not mature to develop future product. Considering the weakness of spot market of China's national ETS, this article concluded pathway and policy recommendations to develop futures market of China's national ETS in three phases.

articleTitle: Control Configuration Based on AOE and Its Application in the Power Allocation of BESSs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As modern industrial control shifts to a more intelligent and distributed system, control configuration technology has become an important method to achieve the control objective. However, the current control configuration technology is limited by high learning cost and long deployment cycles in practical applications. Based on the rich engineering experience in the field of electrical, this paper proposes a novel control configuration technology based on activity on edge network and provides the relevant configuration details. Our method has shown advantages such as intuitiveness, low learning cost, and short deployment cycles over existing control configuration technology, which is validated in a case study with the method directly applied to power allocation of battery energy storage system (BESS).

articleTitle: Hybrid Digital Twin Architecture for Power System Cyber Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a world-first highly configurable, low cost and scalable hybrid digital twin (HDT) established using single board computers to mimic the smart grid physical components and communication network with high fidelity. The HDT system emulates the smart grid cyber-physical system using MATLAB-SIMULINK model (digital) and single board computers (physical). The HDT architecture and communication system design including the network segmentation using configurable network switch and communication protocol using Node-Redis described in detail. The performance of the HDT communication system in terms of round trip time between the digital and physical models and within network components in the physical model is also studied. The development of the HDT will provide a new platform to study the cyber-security vulnerabilities in smart grids and other cyber-physlcal systems.

articleTitle: Flexibility in active distribution networks - modelling a fully coupled multi-energy system in MESMO
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Actively managed and coupled distribution systems in form of multi-energy systems (MES) can play an important role in the efforts to decarbonize the global energy consumption. The Multi-Energy System Modeling and Optimization (MESMO) tool can accelerate research by providing modelling and analysis modules open source. This paper presents the extension of MESMO to allow the simulation of a MES comprising electric, thermal and gas grid which are coupled through conversion units. The implementation is demonstrated in a case study showing different MES configurations in constrained and unconstrained operation.

articleTitle: An EV Charging Scheduling Methodology to Reduce Demand and Energy Charges in Industrial and Commercial Sites
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of plug-in electric vehicles (EVs), peak demand charges can make up a considerable portion of the electricity bills of industrial and commercial sites that host an EV charging station. Typically, daily peak demand minimization-based EV charging scheduling strategies are used to avoid significant demand charges. However, these approaches may lead to suboptimal results for reducing total electricity cost as they do not account for the energy charges and the historical peak values within a billing period. In this work, a receding horizon control-based EV charging scheduling methodology is proposed to simultaneously reduce the demand and energy charges of an industrial/commercial site with an EV charging station. As a salient feature, the methodology maintains data privacy as the confidential power system- and EV-related data are not circulated. Case studies on a workplace charging setting reveal that the proposed methodology is able to minimize the demand and energy charges to a greater extent when compared to conventional strategies.

articleTitle: Fault Current-Constrained Optimal Power Flow on Unbalanced Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the proliferation of distributed generation into distribution networks, the need to consider fault currents in the dispatch problem becomes increasingly relevant. This paper introduces a method for adding fault current constraints into optimal power flow in order to reduce fault currents while minimizing generation cost. The optimal power flow problem is formulated as a single optimization problem with sub-networks representing the faults of interest. Having a single optimization problem allows the decision variables to be coupled across the optimal power flow and the fault current studies without having to iterate over possible solutions. The proposed method is applicable to unbalanced distribution networks, including those with transformers that introduce phase-shifts.

articleTitle: Optimal Charging Site Recommendation and Scheduling for Electric Vehicles Considering User Price Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the mass rollout of electric vehicles (EVs), exploiting the charging flexibility of EVs becomes a promising solution to improve system operational efficiency. It is obvious that the charging behaviors can be influenced by altering the price incentives, whereas the associated optimization problem concerning the matching between controllable EV resources and charging station (CS) scheduling still remains open. In this regard, a two-level EV-CS matching and scheduling model is proposed in this paper. At the upper level, each EV is recommended to a CS based on the energy scheduling plan from the CSs and the price sensitivity of the EVs. The lower level solves the optimal incentive and scheduling problem associated with the CSs and the assigned EVs. Numerical simulations are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks on Deep Neural Network-based Power System Event Classification Models
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Online event classification is essential to strengthening the reliability of the power transmission system. Recently, deep learning based methods have achieved great success in numerous domains such as computer vision and natural language processing. Researchers began to adopt deep learning based methods to solve the power system event identification problem and achieved effective results. However, these previous works do not consider that deep learning models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, potentially influencing real-world applications' reliability. In this paper, we adopt several adversarial attack mechanisms by adding tailored noise signal to the input Phasor Measurement Units (PMU) time series and make the deep learning model misclassify the power system event. This numerical study discloses that current state-of-the-art deep learning based power system event classifiers are extremely vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which may jeopardize the reliability of the power transmission system.

articleTitle: Higher Training Size, Increased Model Complexity or Both: A Novel Decision Framework for Cycle Life Classification of Lithium-Ion Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Among various prognostic and diagnostic applications of lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries, their classification into high and low-cycle life cells is an important application. This paper focuses on two aspects of data-driven classification models: useful features and model complexity. Acquiring data that is rich in valuable features requires time and hardware resources. Moreover, the effectiveness of features varies from one dataset to another. In this paper, we explore these trade-offs using two different datasets. The results show that the lack of training data can be compensated by using a higher complexity of the machine learning model. The decision framework offers exciting insights for emerging businesses in deciding on the vendors by classifying their cells into low and high cycle life with limited training data.

articleTitle: Stochastic Scheduling of Mobile Energy Storage Systems for Transmission System Resilience Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Mobile energy storage systems (MESSs) have significant potential to enhance the resilience of the power transmission system against extreme weather. A novel two-stage model is proposed to schedule the MESSs and recover the transmission networks (PTNs). The first stage determines the on-off state of the generation unit, and MESSs are dispatched in real-time for load recovery at the second stage. The proposed model is formulated as a two-stage mixed integer programming problem, which is solved by a modified Benders decomposition algorithm. Case studies are conducted on the IEEE-RTS 79 test system to show the effectiveness of the proposed method in the resilience enhancement of the transmission systems.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Adaptive AC/DC- Coupled Droop Characteristic in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Droop control has been widely used in DC microgrids, in which nonlinear droop characteristic is implemented to avoid the shortcomings of linear droop. This paper discusses an AC/DC-Coupled droop control strategy where the d-axis current reference is generated directly from the droop characteristic. The multiple parallel converters provide faster bus voltage transient response under this method while the steady-state performance of this method is not compared with traditional nonlinear strategies. This paper compares the voltage regulation performance of this ac/dc-coupled strategy with three conventional nonlinear droop strategies. Optimization is achieved through voltage-shifting and slope-adjusting methods, and the current sharing accuracy is improved on this basis. Finally, simulations of a multi-source multi-load DC MG validate the superior steady-state performance of the ac/dc-coupled method.

articleTitle: Control Structure Related Admittance-Shaping Effects in VSM Controlled Converters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper contributes to understand the admittance-shaping effects of the underlying control loops related to a converter controlled as a virtual synchronous machine. Here, two different voltage controller implementations are investigated with respect to their passivity and damping properties. This involves how the inertia model shapes the admittance of a virtual synchronous machine. Moreover, the sensitivity of inertia model design regarding the considered voltage controller implementations is identified. In addition to controller implementation sensitivities, it is elaborated how passivity properties may be improved by means of adequate filtering methods as well as an adaption in control structure, namely the voltage drop via the virtual stator model.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch-Based Secondary Control for Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In microgrids, the economic dispatch is usually considered in the tertiary control level where the control time constant takes several minutes. Therefore, the loads and renewable energy production is required to be estimated. The estimationbased methods introduce uncertainty to the optimization function that degrades the optimal solution. In this paper, the economic dispatch is integrated with the secondary control in such a way that it provides its functionalities and economic dispatch. An optimization function for secondary control is utilized to minimize the cost of active power generation subjected to frequency and voltage nominal and power rating values. The optimization function is solved in real time on a timescale of 0.5 sec. The proposed controller is simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK and compared with decentralized secondary controller with the objective to restore the frequency and voltage of the microgrid. The proposed controller effectively reduces the cost by 7% as compared to decentralized controller.

articleTitle: A Review of Control Strategies for Operation of Distributed Resources Under Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: India is aiming for 100% electrification of its territories. In the process, many remote locations need to be connected to nearby electricity supply lines. Interconnection of a remote village with the central grid is a very extensive step, which increases the necessity of converter-based generators as many of them are of renewable based sources. These systems show different characteristics from traditional alternator under faults and affect the operation of the protection relay and system stability. Hence it is necessary to have diverse and robust control strategies to ensure the system stability during and post transient faults. In this connection, this paper aims to review the existing control strategies for operation of distributed generators under line to ground fault, the most common fault. The performance of different control strategies are studied and are compared with the help of numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Modeling of the EV dynamic wireless charging load
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The dynamic wireless charging (DWC) system can charge the electric vehicle (EV) as it travels on the road. Compared with the traditional wired charging mode, DWC can reduce range anxiety of the driver, avoid mechanical wear on the charging plug, and does not generate sparks. The analysis of the EV DWC load characteristics in existing studies is insufficient, and there is no detailed dynamic DWC load model. Based on above analysis, this paper firstly analyzes the motor power and battery power characteristics of the EV; Then, the overall EV DWC load model is established based on the coupling of motor power and battery power. Compared to traditional DWC constant power model, the dynamic DWC load model proposed in this paper can more accurately reflect the dynamic power characteristics of the EV during the DWC process.

articleTitle: Mobile Vehicle to Microgrid for Emergency Distribution System Operation Considering EV SOCs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With recent advancements in electric vehicles (EVs) and autonomous driving, the development of transportation and power systems has attracted significant attention. Specifically, vehicle-to-grid (V2G) systems, which use EVs instead of battery energy storage systems (BESSs), have been extensively studied. In this study, we assume a scenario wherein an accident occurs in the upper section of the distribution system, and the restoration becomes difficult. Power failure restoration was performed by composing a mobile vehicle-to-microgrid (V2MG) using EVs as mobile resources in the power-failure section of the distribution system. Electric power can be sustainably supplied by a power-supply vehicle with a rotating machine as well as EVs. The charge/discharge powers of the EVs are controlled considering uncertainties of EV locations and states of charge.

articleTitle: Impact of non-idealities on Control of Ultracapacitor based Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Ultracapacitor based energy storage systems are becoming increasingly popular for applications requiring short-term support. This paper investigates the impact of non-idealities on and control of ultracapacitor-based energy storage systems. The impact of two non-idealities, namely, the equivalent series resistance and the voltage-dependent capacitance, has been studied in detail. The typical variation of capacitance as a function of voltage is experimentally determined, and its impact on the controller design is studied. Further, the challenges arising due to equivalent series resistance in adopting a dual loop control, especially during the charging mode, are reported. The oscillatory response resulting due to equivalent series resistance is demonstrated experimentally using a 24 V laboratory prototype comprising of 10 series connected ultracapacitors.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Weak Grid Interfaced Microgrid Using Multi Generalized Integrator Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Grid interfaced converter (GIC) is a crucial element in microgrids for efficient utilization of the generated electrical energy. The microgrid plants are situated in far distances from the load centers, which are eventually integrated into weak utility grid. Therefore, synchronization and efficient power flow together with improved quality become the fundamental criteria when choosing a control strategy. This paper proposes a multi-generalized integrator-based control strategy to improve the power transfer capabilities of a weak grid interfaced microgrid. The vital parameters considered here are, dc-offset rejection, power quality, and unity power factor operation under various modes of microgrid operation. All theoretical implications of the proposed controller are examined through numerical simulations by testing the controller for various conditions of grid, load, and microgrid operations. The simulation results substantiate the efficacy of the proposed controller during the adverse conditions of the utility grid and increased power flow from microgrid sources.

articleTitle: Trajectory Based Model Predictive Control Strategy for LC Filtered VSIs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In order to improve dynamic response of the voltage source inverter in ac microgrids, model predictive control becomes a promising alternative. This paper proposes a trajectory based model predictive control, which provides a concise approach to improving the total harmonic distortion and root-mean-square error. Meanwhile, a carrier-based modulation method is applied to further simplify the calculation. Simulations results demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposal <tex>$\mathbf{in}$</tex> different load and switching frequency conditions.

articleTitle: Potential impact of wind-based Synthetic Inertia on the Frequency Response of the Argentine-Uruguayan Interconnected Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy sources has motivated a growing interest on the frequency response of the electrical power systems in scenarios with reduced inertia and on control strategies to cope with them. Among other technically feasible solutions, synthetic inertia strategies has proven to be a valuable solution that take advantage of the installed wind power. This paper describes the implementation of a PSS/E (Power System Simulator for Engineering) model of synthetic inertia for wind generators and its use for the assessment of the impact that this control strategy, implemented on the Uruguayan wind generators, may achieve for the Argentine-Uruauayan interconnected power system.

articleTitle: A Linear Probabilistic Optimal Power Flow Model with Linearization Error Checking
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the integration of renewable energy, probabilistic optimal power flow (POPF) becomes an important tool to analyze system uncertainty. To relieve the computational burden of POPF, a linear OPF model is proposed. To make the linear OPF accurate, an optimization method is proposed to obtain the worst-case error of the used linear power flow (LPF) model. When the worst-case error is unacceptable, a min-max two-levels optimization problem is proposed to obtain the optimal LPF model (i.e., in terms of minimizing the worst-case error) over a defined linearization range. To solve the difficult min-max problem, an analytical approximation method is proposed to reformulate the min-max problem as a tractable one-level linear program. By applying the error checking, the proposed linear OPF yields better solutions. Several standard systems are tested and the results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Community Energy Cooperation with Shared Energy Storage for Economic-Environment Benefits
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Community energy management is critical for facilitating the transition towards sustainable and clean smart grids. Energy cooperation techniques with community shared energy storage should be developed to reduce the challenges of distributed energy resources' uncertain and variable nature to a reliable power system. The proposed coordinator-users model involves the coordinator for techno-economic-environment optimization to minimize the community energy cost and carbon dioxide emissions. The end-users, including consumers and prosumers, also can make self-driven decisions to reduce their energy costs and contribute to a low-carbon society. By complementing the model with demand response dissatisfaction cost to evaluate the willingness of the user to participate in the energy cooperation, the techno-economic-environment-satisfaction benefit can be optimized at the community and user level. The effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed model are evaluated with the real-world dataset. The improvements in economic and environmental benefits are significant.

articleTitle: Optimal sizing of Battery Energy Storage Systems for self-consumption in Urban Micro-grids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the increased adoption of distributed energy resources in the urban context, there is a growing potential for the realization of grid-connected networked micro-grids that can facilitate the collective utilization of local energy resources. The coordination of different flexibilities in the generation and demand side, complemented by energy storage systems is required for efficient local energy management. This work discusses a study on the sizing of battery energy storage systems for optimizing the overall return on such investment on the local scale and the planning of its operation for such self-consumption and market participation use cases. The simulation studies have been conducted based on historical wholesale electricity price data of the region.

articleTitle: Review on China's National Carbon Market and Analysis for Commercial Development Potential of Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage in China
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) has been deemed as a necessary choice of the last mile in realizing carbon neutrality. Currently, the high cost of CCUS is still a major barrier for commercialization. In this review, we hope to explore the commercial development potentials of CCUS in China basing on carbon trading mechanism, and meanwhile clarify the key factors impacting the commercialization of CCUS. CCUS is proved to be increasingly important for China's carbon emission reduction from 2025 to 2060, and was predicted to contribute a CO<inf>2</inf> emission reduction potential of around 9~30 million tons of CO<inf>2</inf> in 2025, and this figure will increase up to 1~1.82 billion tons in 2060. There are two key factors affecting the commercialization of CCUS, including carbon price and if CO<inf>2</inf> stored by CCUS projects cane been recognized as carbon credit.

articleTitle: Detection of Bad Data and False Data Injection Based on Back-Propagation Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Power system state estimation is an essential tool for monitoring the operating conditions of the grid. However, the collected measurements may not always be reliable due to bad data from various faults as well as the increasing potential of being exposed to cyber-attacks, particularly from data injection attacks. To enhance the accuracy of state estimation, this paper presents a back-propagation neural network to detect and identify bad data and false data injections. A variety of training data exhibiting different statistical properties were used for training. The developed strategy was tested on the IEEE 30-bus and 118-bus power systems using MATLAB. Simulation results revealed the feasibility of the method for the detection and differentiation of bad data and false data injections in various operating scenarios.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Ice Blockage Estimation of Water Intake at Niagara Hydropower Station
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Frazil ice and anchor ice could cause ice blockage at water intakes, which results in shutting down intake facilities and/or lowering the active power output of the hydropower plant. This paper proposes a data-driven ice blockage estimation method for the water intake. Specifically, the flow velocity coefficient of the conduit is calculated from water levels at the water intake and forebay, and water flows at hydropower units in conjunction with the water storage and leveraged as the index for ice blockage. Detection conditions and rejection conditions are showcased to extract only highly probable ice blockage events and exclude false positives, respectively. The ice blockage estimation performance was examined with eleven years of historical data at Niagara hydropower stations. System operation logs demonstrate that the anchor ice, lake ice, and shore ice were continuously observed 4–15 hours before the three detected occurrences, which serve as evidence of the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of Air-conditioning Load and Battery Energy Storage System for Improving Electricity Supply-demand Balancing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In the day-ahead electricity market, the next day's demand is scheduled one day before. Deviations from the forecasted demand on the day of operation results in costly penalties for the retailer. This study proposes a method for coordinating the operation of a Heating Ventilation and Air-conditioning (HVAC) load and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) to reduce the occurrence of the imbalance. The proposed method changes the HVAC operation within the comfortability range of indoor temperature when demand forecast error is low and uses the changed power to charge/discharge BESS. When a significant forecast error occurs, the charged/discharged energy in BESS in a prior period is also used in addition to HVAC load adjustment to suppress the imbalance further. In a sample simulation, the average load imbalance of 6.6% was eliminated with the proposed method, whereas it was only reduced to 5.4% with HVAC curtailment alone.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Phase Multilevel Inverter Cascaded by Three-Phase Two-Level Inverter and Two Single-Phase Boosted H-Bridge Inverters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: A novel three-phase 9-level inverter topology formed by cascading two H-bridge inverters (HBIs) and two-level three-phase inverter (TTI) with voltage boosting feature using PWM switching technique has been presented in this paper. This topology utilizes three symmetrical DC-sources and four switched-capacitors (SCs), which are self-balanced within a switching duration. Compared with Cascaded-MLI (CMLI), the proposed inverter topology has advantages of better utilisation of DC-sources, less number of power electronics devices, and gate-driver circuits without compromising the performance of the inverter. The validity of the proposed topology is examined through MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Integration of Demand Side Flexibility Resources in Distribution Network Planning with High Penetration of PV
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the gradual increase of the load capacity in the distribution network, the capacity of the distribution network lines in the power grid tends to be insufficient, and the lines need to be expanded. The popularization of demand side flexibility resources in virtual power plants(VPP) and the large-scale application of energy storage provide solutions to the above problems. In this paper,a two-layer planning model of distribution network that comprehensively considers the demand side flexibility resources of VPP and combined output of photovoltaics and storage is proposed. The Garver-6 bus system is taked in this paper as an example to carry out distribution network planning. The results of the calculation example shows that the addition of the demand side flexibility resources and energy storage reduces the planning cost of the distribution network, and also improves the consumption rate of photovoltaics. It can provide reference for future power system planning.

articleTitle: Distributed Hierarchical Control for VSC-Based DC Microgrids with AC-DC Coupled Strategy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes an ac-dc coupled distributed hierarchical control strategy for VSC-based de microgrids (MGs), which directly links the load sharing performance of the MG with the ac inner current (i<inf>d</inf>) control of VSCs. In the primary layer of the hierarchical control, an ac-dc coupled droop method is used, which does not require any outer dc voltage/current PI loops. In the secondary layer, the dc bus voltage is restored while maintaining the precise load sharing performance among sources. Moreover, the feedback current of the secondary layer is obtained from the nonlinear disturbance observer without additional current measurements. Stability analysis of the ac-dc coupled hierarchical control is performed by the established state space model. Case studies are conducted by simulations to demonstrate the performance of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: PPO-based Pricing Method for Shared Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The shared energy storage system has the potential to promote the popularity of the battery energy storage system (BESS). In a shared energy storage system, prosumers could rent capacity and optimize its operation, whereas the operator also seeks to maximize the revenue of the BESS from both rental service and the virtual power plant (VPP) market. To optimize the pricing policy of the BESS, a novel pricing method based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is proposed for this energy storage rental service. The interaction between the BESS operator and prosumers is formulated as a bi-level optimization problem, which is further reformulated as a Markov decision process (MDP) and solved through the proximal policy optimization (PPO)-based DRL method. The case study shows that the proposed method could further increase the revenues of the BESS operator.

articleTitle: Suitability Assessment of Flywheel Energy Storage Systems for providing new Frequency Response Services in the UK
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: National Grid ESO has recently introduced three new frequency response services to the UK electricity market. The three services are Dynamic Containment (DC), Dynamic Regulation (DR) and Dynamic Moderation (DM). Each service has individual performance requirements and restrictions. This paper looks for the first time at how Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESSs) can be used to supply these services. Sensitivity analyses have been performed for each service to assess the suitability of FESSs of differing C-Rates to participate. It has been demonstrated that a FESS rated up to 18C is able to provide an average availability above 95% when performing high and low DC simultaneously, with the same threshold being reached up to 4C for DM. None of the C-Rates analysed were able to reach this threshold when performing DR. Hybridisation is shown to introduce performance benefits to the systems, allowing higher C-Rate systems to reach the 95% threshold than when performing individually.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning based Voltage Control on Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Due to the high penetration of renewable energy in the distribution network, the exponential increase in the amount of data collected and variables makes it difficult for centralized control methods to achieve real-time voltage regulation. Besides, hardware conditions (e.g., communication equipment) limit its application in practice. Therefore, a model-free multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) voltage control strategy is developed in this paper. The proposed MADRL control strategy is carried out with a framework of centralized training and distributed execution. We apply deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm to help each agent control its corresponding PV inverter in a distributed manner. However, during the training process, the agent could observe other agents' information to improve training. The simulation on a 33-bus distribution network is carried out to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, and its superiority is also validated by comparing with traditional methods.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Configuration of Battery Energy Storage System for Photovoltaic Systems with Different Load Demand
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Under the goal of carbon neutrality, the installed capacity of photovoltaic power generation would increase rapidly in the next few years, and the demand for battery energy storage would increase accordingly for its effects on smoothening the renewable power output and increasing the consumption rate of renewable generation. To achieve the balance between the consumption rate of renewable generation and initial investment on BESS, a novel optimal configuration method of BESS for photovoltaic systems is proposed. The practical statistical data and simulation data are adopted for the tests to validate the performance of the proposed method. And several comparative analyses are carried out to demonstrate the influence of different factors, such as load demand curves, TOU prices, and load levels. The effects of BESS on the annual costs are also illustrated. The proposed method can help customers to design the combined photovoltaic and BESS systems in a more economical way.

articleTitle: Power loss reduction in distribution systems in the presence of DGs and EVs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The rapidly increasing demand for electrical power and difficulties in providing the same using traditional power generating sources provide a motivation to integrate Distributed Generation (DG) into the radial distribution network. In the present work, the optimal installation of DG along with operation of Electric Vehicles (EV) is investigated on standard IEEE distribution systems for minimizing network power losses. This also helps in simultaneous improvement of voltage profile of the network. The optimal positioning and power rating of DG are computed by Genetic Algorithm (GA). In the presence of EV, the loads are variable due to the charging and discharging of batteries in the EV. The variation of network power losses in the presence of EVs along with DGs on standard IEEE 33 and 69 Bus systems are investigated.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Enhancement Through Active Power Control of Converter-Interfaced Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The paper investigates the ability of Converter-Interfaced Generators (CIGs) to improve the stability margin of power systems by adjusting their active power injections at their points of connection. To this aim, a voltage magnitude-active power control scheme is examined and its effectiveness is tested considering different topology and CIG reactive power capability scenarios. The focus is on the effect on long-term voltage instabilities due to the system reaching its loadability limit, as well as on small-disturbance, short-term instabilities, arising in the form of Hopf bifurcations. Simulation results are based on a continuation power flow analysis carried out considering a modified version of the IEEE 39-bus system, where a portion of synchronous machines is replaced by CIGs.

articleTitle: A Gramian Angular Field Transform-Based Higher-Dimension Data-Driven Method for Post-Fault Short-Term Voltage Stability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As the complexity of power systems increases, together with the increasing integration of phasor measurement units, an intelligent assessment for short-term voltage stability (STVS) becomes necessary and feasible. Especially for post-fault STVS assessment, the task requires a fast and accurate conclusion. Given this, an intelligent post-fault STVS assessment method is proposed in this research. Based on Gramian Angular Field transform, two-dimensional convolutional neural network, and adaptive confidence interval, the proposed method with an offline-online data-driven framework shows better performance when the amount of input data is limited. The related simulations are conducted on the New England 10-machine 39-bus system.

articleTitle: Resilience-oriented Modeling and Co-optimization for Coupled Power and Water Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The interdependencies between the power distribution system (PDS) and water distribution system (WDS) are well-acknowledged in resilience analysis. Such interdependencies can hinder the post-disruption service restoration of both systems, and prolong the overall recovery process. Aimed at handling these issues, this paper proposes a resilience-oriented modeling and co-optimization method for coupled power and water (CPW) systems. The model integrates critical features of modern CPW systems, such as microgrids and distributed generations for power and water treatment plants, pumps, and tanks, for the water side. The interdependencies are extracted and formulated from mutual demand aspects. Further, a multi-objective optimization is presented to simultaneously reduce the loss of power load (LOPL) and loss of water load (LOWL). Finally, the method is tested on a coupled 33-bus power and 25-node water system and the result demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Approach for Frequency Response Prediction in Low Inertia Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The uncertainty in securely operating the power system has increased with large-scale integration of inverter based resources (IBRs). IBR-driven displacement of conventional sources results in diminishing inherent frequency support capability of such systems as, unlike conventional synchronous generators, IBRs do not inherently support the grid frequency. Therefore, with increasing vulnerability, there is a need for an accurate frequency prediction model that could help a grid operator better plan system resources and securely operate the power system. Against this backdrop, this paper initially provides a critical insight into the frequency response of IBR-dominated systems to highlight the limitation of using a linear prediction model. Following the critical analysis, the paper proposes a data extraction framework and XGBoost algorithm-based regression model to predict RoCoF, frequency nadir, and quassi steady-state frequency of the IBR-dominated power system. The proposed approach has been implemented on a modified IEEE-39 bus system, and its comparative analysis with other state-of-art algorithms supports the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Smart Charging of Electric Vehicles at Residence Under Different Tariff Regimes and Meter Configurations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Despite being the world's third-largest emitter of Carbon Dioxide, India's ambitious pledge at the Conference of Parties (COP-26) to attain Net Zero Carbon Emissions by 2070 needs to be backed by a concrete action plan. This paper highlights the various options available with an Electric Vehicle (EV) owner to charge the vehicle at the residence. Choosing the best available option as per the owners' convenience will not only reduce the financial burden but also increase the efficiency of the grid by effectively addressing the critical issues such as ‘peak shaving’ and ‘valley filling’ as the number of EVs on the road increase in days to come. In the long run, this reduces the emission of Green House Gases(GHG) and carbon footprint. These proposals are backed with the results obtained from MATLAB simulation and sound calculations.

Author Keywords: ToD Tariff and Residential Charging of Electric Vehicle

articleTitle: PV-Grid Interface Hybrid Energy Management System for EV Charging Station without PLL
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Electric vehicles are gaining popularity as an environmentally benign, long-term, and cost-effective alternative to internal combustion engines based automobiles. It deals with depleting fuel, climate crisis, and pollution. The proposed work focuses on designing a PV grid interface hybrid energy management system for EV-charging stations without using a PLL synchronizing unit. The above methodology ensures that the system functions to optimize grid energy utilisation. The power from PV is extracted via Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). Various operating modes are observed depending on the amount of power available at the PV and the power demand at the charging station. The power may flow from PV to charging station and utility or from PV and grid to charging station depending upon the power availability and demand scenario. The power injection or absorption capability of the converter is significantly affected in presence of a weak grid. The paper provides the details regarding the power electronics-based converter model and their respective controller design that are used in the system.

articleTitle: Study on the Financial Settlement of Textile Printing and Dyeing Enterprises in the Carbon Trading Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Due to the lack of calculating standards, as the highest carbon emissions enterprises in the textile industry, printing and dyeing companies are facing a difficult situation when choosing their accounting treatment. In order to help these enterprises to enter the carbon trading market for the first time to choose the appropriate accounting calculation method, we analyze the financial settlement of carbon emission rights and carbon allowances by conducting in-depth survey for real printing and dyeing companies. Then, from the perspective of the relationship between the carbon emissions of enterprises, the pricing when purchasing carbon allowances, and the accounting treatment of enterprises, we propose a prediction model of the financial data and profit as well as loss situation of enterprises' carbon trading under different choices. Furthermore, directional reference for the accounting practice operation of printing and dyeing enterprises are suggested in this study, which will help printing and dyeing enterprises successfully realize the transformation of energy saving and emission reduction.

articleTitle: Stochastic Unit Commitment Model Considering the Impact of Carbon Emissions Trading
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Carbon emission is the most fundamental factor leading to global warming. Countries around the world are actively building carbon emission trading (CET) markets. Based on China's CET policy, a two-stage stochastic unit commitment model is established to analyze the impact of CET on power systems. Case studies on China's actual power system are performed to analyze the impact of CET policies, carbon prices, and carbon emission coefficients on carbon emission reduction and renewable energy consumption.

articleTitle: Trading Strategy for Renewable Energy Sources in Day-Ahead and Continuous Intraday Market
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Electricity produced by weather dependent renewable energy sources (RES) like wind, solar PV etc. is intermittent. Accuracy of forecasting renewable generation is higher for shorter forecasting horizons. Therefore, RES prefer to trade in intraday continuous markets where trading happens relatively closer to the delivery time. However, trading in one market solely may prevent a RES from utilizing the opportunities presented by the other market. In this paper, we propose a strategy for RES to trade in the day-ahead as well as intraday markets. Our method suggests a percentage allocation of RES generation to trade in the two markets considering their market price fluctuations and associated risks. We test the efficacy of our approach on real world day-ahead and intra-day market logs obtained from the European Power Exchange (EPEX). We find that our proposed trading strategy yields an improvement of nearly 20% over intuitive baselines in terms of revenue earned.

articleTitle: Phasor Domain Single-Ended Transmission Line Fault Location Method Based on Harmonics without Remote Side Information
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Based on the harmonics within the power system, in this paper, a phasor domain single-ended transmission line fault location method is proposed. The method does not require communication channels from the remote terminal, and works without remote side voltages, currents, or source impedances. First, the apparent impedance at the fundamental frequency seen by the relay at the local terminal is presented. Second, with the apparent impedance at an example harmonic, additional information is introduced to the fault location problem, resulting in 4 real equations and 4 real unknowns. Finally, the unknowns are solved via Newton's method, including the fault location. Numerical experiments verify that the proposed single-ended fault location method presents higher fault location accuracy compared to the existing single-ended fault location method without remote side information in <sup>t</sup>he IEEE C37.114 standard, with different fault types and fault locations.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Optimization Framework for Battery Energy Storage System Co-Optimization in Regulation Market
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: We propose a two-stage model predictive control (MPC) based optimization framework to enable regulation market participation for battery energy storage systems (BESSs). Specifically, the first stage of the optimization, named “Stage-A”, aims to compute optimal charging and discharging power references for the BESS. The second stage, named “Stage-B”, aims to track the regulation signal closely, while working in conjunction with Stage-A. The proposed framework can be readily extended to multiple number of BESSs and can be also configured to support different regulation market models. We consider Singapore regulation market as a case study and show that the model can strictly abide by market rules of state of charge (SOC) based basepoint setting and prevention of reverse behavior, while following the regulation signal closely.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Islanding and Grid Reconnection capability of a microgrid within distribution system
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Microgrid can operate in either islanded or grid connected mode. It acts as a single controllable unit in the grid connected mode and operates as an independent grid in the islanded mode. A microgrid controller orchestrates the operation of distributed energy resources (DERs), load, voltage regulation devices and distribution automation switches to ensure a stable operation of microgrid in both modes. A safe and reliable mode transitioning requires proper coordination between the DERs and distribution automation (DA) devices. This paper presents the lessons learned from a microgrid islanding and reconnection test performed by ComEd. It discusses the overall approach of testing, preparations and testbed setup, and test results of seamless islanding and grid reconnection of a microgrid.

articleTitle: Analysis on Motivation of Textile Printing and Dyeing Enterprises to Participate in Carbon Trading in China
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Global warming is a universal challenge faced by mankind. Carbon trading is a market based mechanism adopted to promote the reduction of greenhouse gas emission. This paper analyzes the motivation of Chinese enterprises of textile printing and dyeing to participate in carbon trading, and discusses the relationship between current situation and motivation of those enterprises, so as to help relevant departments make strategic planning to encourage enterprises to participate carbon trading, and provide the textile industry a reference of carbon market operation. In this paper, six textile printing and dyeing enterprises in China with different economic size and main products are selected as the research objects for in-depth interviews for their real practice in carbon trading. Content coding method is used to analyze and cluster verification of first-hand interview data, so as to build a driving model for Chinese textile enterprises to participate in carbon trading.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Battery Energy Storage and Gas Turbine for Ancillary Service Provision
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Ancillary services play a crucial role in maintaining the reliability of electrical power grids with integrated intermittent renewable energy generation. They can also provide additional revenue streams for systems with distributed energy resources (DERs), e.g., battery energy storage systems (BESSs) and gas turbines (GTs). This paper evaluates the benefits of the joint optimization and coordinated control of the BESS and GT for energy arbitrage and ancillary services provision. Specifically, we mathematically model a system with BESS and GT and formulate an optimization problem to maximize the profit through participation in various markets. As a case study, we consider participation in Singapore's wholesale electricity market for energy arbitrage, regulation, and contingency reserve. Our analysis based on Singapore's actual market prices shows that the complimentary nature of BESS and GT can be leveraged for additional revenue through participation in both fast-response regulation market and a relatively slower-response but longer-term contingency reserve market.

articleTitle: Coordinated Operation Scheduling Method of Distribution Grid and Microgrids with Gradient Estimation by Finite Difference
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Photovoltaics installation causes voltage deviations at distribution grids (DGs). The coordinated operation of a DG and microgrids (MGs) eliminates the voltage deviations at lower cost than grid-facility reinforcement. Conventional operation scheduling methods require that MG operators (MGOs) send gradient of their objective function to the DG operator (DGO), whereas not all MGOs can calculate the gradient information. To address this issue, a coordinated operation scheduling method that uses Benders decomposition with gradient estimation is proposed. With this method, the DGO receives only energy cost from MGOs and estimates the gradient information on the basis of the second-order central difference method, which is a kind of finite difference methods. The proposed method has an advantage that the DGO can make coordination with more MGOs and secure more flexibility to eliminate voltage deviations at the DG. A numerical experiment was conducted with a modified IEEE 34 bus feeder with three MGs. The results indicate that the proposed method can eliminate voltage-constraint violations by coordinating with MGs that have no calculation capability of gradient information.

articleTitle: Demand Analysis and Practice of Zero-Carbon Industrial Parks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Specific requirements for the control of global average temperature increase were put forward in the Paris Agreement. China has proposed the 3060 Goal of “emission peaking” and “carbon neutrality”. In addition, the development goals set by China requires that GDP and related primary energy demand maintain a high growth, which brings great challenges to the realization of the “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality” goal. Among them, the carbon emissions of industrial parks in China account for nearly 40% of the total emissions across the country, showing a rising trend. How to balance the coordinated, unified and sustainable development of ecological civilization, scientific and technological innovation and economic prosperity has become an urgent problem for China's industrial parks. This paper analyses the macro and micro problems existing in the process of carbon emission reduction in industrial parks, and their potential and advantages in: industry, function, innovation, mechanism, ability, etc., and then provides a concrete exposition by constructing the standard system of zero-carbon park and developing the zero-carbon operating system that can be used in practice, in order to realize a solution of energy transformation in industrial parks.

Index Terms: Increase In The Global Average Temperature

articleTitle: Reconfiguration Based Load Restoration in Active Distribution Networks with A Voltage Frequency Dependent Load Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Distribution network reconfiguration has been widely applied to enhance resilience of active distribution networks (ADNs) after extreme contingency events. While distributed generation (DG) units are connected to the network after network reconfiguration, uncertain loads and renewable power outputs may cause power imbalance and frequency deviation in each islanded network. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a reconfiguration method considering system frequency and a practical voltage frequency dependent load model. In addition, this paper considers the full reconfiguration potential that each branch has one switch to be controlled more flexibly, thus restoring loads to the maximal level. To address the proposed intractable load restoration problem, an advanced alternative optimization algorithm is proposed. Thus, a resilience enhancement method for ADNs under the post-event state is proposed. Case study conducted on a 33-bus system verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method on load restoration with consideration of uncertainty realizations and frequency deviations.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Generation Schedule Considering Community Microgrid's Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Recently, a community microgrid (MG) has been attracted solution for managing a local area energy network. The proposed robust generation schedules are carried out to evaluate the performance of the MG system operation. The authors have already developed the fundamental system operation and planning functions which was named robust supply and demand manager. The effectiveness of the proposed manager is demonstrated for the MG including photovoltaic generations (PVs), battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and electric vehicles (EVs). The approach for mitigating the irregularity associated with the uncertainties of PVs, EVs, and BESSs' behavior is developed in this paper.

articleTitle: Impact of Solar Generation Unit on the Static Stability of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The main goal of renewable energy is to ensure global access to inexpensive and reliable energy sources, a high level of environmental and climatic safety, as well as to improve the reliability and efficiency of power supply of consumers. However, penetration level of renewable generation also has a great impact on the stability of the system. In particular, based on the power electronic interface renewable unit impacts on the processes in system, changes its frequency spectrum and increases the potential for the appearance of new operation modes of power system. The analysis of the static stability of system with different penetration level of solar generation unit is shown in this paper. The results of studies of loading in normal and post-emergency modes of power system, calculation of static stability margin of active power and voltage, and analysis of damping properties of power system without and with renewable units are presented.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Voltage and Current Control of Four Leg Inverter for Micro-grids and Distributed Generation Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced model predictive voltage and current control of a three phase two level four leg inverter. Commercially trusted PI control strategy experience the arbitration of steady state and transient performance. Also the PI controller gain parameters are not optimal for the whole control operation space. So as to upgrade the control resilience of the converter, a new Model predictive control(MPC) is proposed. MPC is well acknowledged for its superior dynamic performance, intuitiveness, multi objective and multi constrain treatment. However, the basic FCS-MPC (Finite Control Set MPC) develops a variable switching frequency which leads to difficulties in filter design and poor THD performance. So a fixed switching frequency algorithm is implemented by including a virtual modulator based on a predefined switching sequence. Simultaneously, the switch redundancy has been enforced to eliminate the weight factor coupled between load voltage and load current. Simulation results are presented and compared to highlight the performance of the proposed MPC.

articleTitle: Implementation of DC-DC Converter using Ultra Capacitor and Digital Controller for Battery Electric vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Due to the increasing cost of fossil fuels and other non-renewable resources, Environmental conditions and higher capacity accumulator's transformation method has been changing day by day. Though modern controllers are adopted in Electric vehicles, the primary source of battery which causes error and need to enhance the parameters. In this paper, an Improvement of the dynamic performance of the Battery Electric drive is presented. Here DC-DC Converter with different topologies has been compared for the performance of Electric Vehicles. Battery current ripples and converter losses which creates problem in Electric vehicles. Hence Improved SEPIC Converter is designed for the improvement of Electric vehicles. The Conventional linear controllers such Proportional Integral and Derivative (PID) which require analytical modeling system. Besides a Digital Controller FPGA is complete opposite PID which is based trial and error method, and doesn't include any mathematical analyze modeling of the system. However the FPGA is more sturdy (tough), has more strong study state response, and it is able to attain transient and steady state response as compared to PID controllers. The above approach is applied and experimented with simulation software for the performance the SEPIC (DC to DC converter) is discussed here in this research. Finally, the investigations of selected drive performance such as Battery Voltage, Current, Ultra Capacitor current and PID Controllers parameters and digital controllers Evaluation Parameters are presented here.

articleTitle: Evolution of Electricity Distribution Control Room Data Streams - UK Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The move towards ‘Net Zero’, the balance of greenhouse gas emissions produced and removed from the atmosphere, is increasing the complexity of managing distribution networks, with more deployments of low carbon technologies, new markets for flexibility services, and greater monitoring and visibility of the network itself. This has driven the UK's Distribution Network Operators who manage the network, to evolve towards becoming Distribution System Operators, taking on a role more akin to the traditionally more complex Transmission System Operator. In parallel with this development, the data streams utilised by the distribution network control room have also evolved. This paper sets out this evolution by detailing the existing data streams within a typical distribution control room, and how these data streams will need to evolve, as well what new sources of data a future control room will need to accommodate, and finally by identifying novel ways that that value can be created from this data through the use of new ‘smart’ tools.

articleTitle: Transient stability improvement of Croatian power system using FACTS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In the last twenty years, the share of renewable energy sources (RES) in total electricity production has increased significantly, which has led to certain problems in power system operation. In systems with a significant share of RES, connected to the transmission network via power electronics devices, the inertial response of the system is reduced. Due to the reduced inertia of the power system, synchronous generators are more sensitive to their disturbed states and as a result, can easily lose stability. Loss of stability of one generator can lead to failure of other system elements, which may ultimately result in partial or even complete breakdown of the power system. Recently, a large increase in production from renewable sources has been recorded in the Croatian power system, therefore this paper investigates their impact on the system's transient stability and the possibilities of its improvement using Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS).

articleTitle: Real Time Detection and Control of Loss of Synchronism using Energy Function Criterion and Phase Sequence Exchange Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Transient instability is a well-known problem in a power grids. The severe faults in the power grid may lead to blackout, if proper out-of-step protection is not implemented. Phase sequence exchange (PSE) is a newly developed emergency control technique, in which power electronic devices are used to change the phase sequence, thereby reducing the power angle of an equivalent dual power supply system by 120° and preventing the system from becoming unstable. This paper proposes a fast and accurate technique for controlling PSE devices by generating switching signals using local measurement after detection of unstable swings and shows the effectiveness of PSE in stabilizing a multi-machine system. The proposed technique uses energy function for determining unstable swing. The proposed technique has been tested on the IEEE 39-bus test system on a real-time digital simulator (RTDS), and the results show that the proposed control technique for the PSE device is effective.

articleTitle: Info of invited presentation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The secure operation of low-voltage power systems highly relies on thedemand-side flexibility to follow the variability and uncertainty in the renewable distributed generation. On the other hand, the flexibility from network side has been paid less attention. In this study, we reinvestigate optimal power flow problems indistribution systems and microgrids bycombining network-side flexibility in the formof line switching or soft line parameter adjustment. The former one is usually referred to as network reconfiguration and the latter one is enabled by installing line-based power electronic devices such as power flow routers. Via both analytical and numerical studies, we reveal that demand-side flexibility and network-sideflexibility take complementary effects in accommodating renewable energy. Demand-side flexibilitymainly tunes the forecast-scenario operating point,while network-side flexibilitycontributes to reducing the degree of voltage fluctuation under renewable uncertainty,showing that network-side flexibility is a promising resource in future grids.

articleTitle: Towards Making Intelligent Decisions on SOC Strategies for EV Battery Life Enhancement under Practical DoD Ranges
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The battery pack is the primary energy source in Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) and must be carefully managed. The driving profile and operational SOC impact the life of the battery pack. In this paper, we investigate the impact of operational SOC strategies on the residual capacity of the EV battery pack for different test driving profiles. We have chosen fixed distance and fixed degradation methodologies to determine suitable SOC strategies for enhanced lifecycle. The results show that a depth of discharge (DoD) in the range of 40–60% is practical for all the drive profiles. Moreover, Highway Fuel Economy Test (HWFET) provides us with the minimum degradation and covers the maximum distance, while for the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure ((WLTP)), the battery degrades relatively quicker. Furthermore, the SOC strategy with higher DoD must be avoided for an enhanced life cycle or an increased distance for the same degradation.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Grid Connected SPCS under Unbalanced Grid Voltage, Frequency Deviation and Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper presents the performance analysis of double stage solar power conversion system (SPCS) connected to the grid via three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI). Integration of large numbers of solar photovoltaic (PV) system has raised the power quality issues under various operating environment. Accurate grid synchronization, current reference generation for the controller and reducing the harmonics contents has become factor of concern for electrical power quality. The functionality of power controller, double second order generalize integrator (DSOGI)-phase locked loop (PLL) and proportional resonator-harmonic compensator <tex>$(PR+HC)$</tex> is verified under unbalanced grid voltage, frequency deviation and load current harmonics. The simulation results shows the active power from SPCS is injected into the grid at unity power factor and grid current profile is improved with THD of 2.55%. The proposed system incorporating <tex>$PR+HC$</tex> controller, tracks the reference signal and removes the dominant 5<sup>th</sup> and 7<sup>th</sup> harmonics from the load current.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling in Rural Community Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The cost of connecting remote rural villages in China to the main power grid can be high due to geographical and population constraints. In such cases, it could be more economical to establish community microgrids, and tap into the local renewable resources. This paper studies the feasibility of operating islanded microgrids for rural villages. Three Chinese villages were selected, and simulation models were constructed to model their electrical consumption patterns. Subsequently, a multi-objective optimal dispatching model is proposed to minimize the operating costs as well as any associated environmental impacts. Numerical findings conducted in MATLAB show that community microgrid is a feasible option for rural electrification in China.

articleTitle: Modified Triple-port Inductor based Dual Boost DC-DC Converter for Single Phase PV System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The integration small scale solar photovoltaic (PV) system existing utility grid is always a challenging task because of low in voltage level at DC bus. So that improve the level of voltage and easy transportation of electrical power three-port switched inductor based double boost DC-DC converter fed single-phase micro-inverter is introduced.
