Blockchains application in methodology on CCER for distributed PV power generation can decrease the cost of management, simplify the certification procedure and ensure the authenticity, security and traceability.

articleTitle: Battery based renewable energy source grid-connected generation system with Improved Power Quality Feature
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The proposed paper has objective to show the solar power has poor quality inverted AC output, if it is merely using power conversion approach from DC to AC. If it is not regulated and controlled properly, the poor quality power would be supplied to the grid as well as to the load. The paper presents a battery-based renewable energy source grid connected generation system (RES-GGS) with improved power quality feature. The power quality is improved by using two stage power conversion approaches. The solar power is extracted at maximum power point tracking (MPPT) using conventional approach and further regulated by DC-DC converter. The cascaded H-bridge inverter is used to give AC output for non-linear load as well as to the grid. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated under varying irradiation condition. The simulated results show improvement of power quality features.

articleTitle: Enabling Trusted Peer-to-Peer Microgrid Energy Transactions during High-Impact Low Probability Weather Events
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Existing technology management strategies to address the electricity distribution system resilience, are utilizing distributed energy resources (DERs) and hardening the network assets during High Impact Weather events (HIW). The retail market mechanism platform for multiple DERs during a power outage caused by the HIW events has not been discussed in the existing literature. This paper focuses on peer-to-peer (P2P) transactive energy platform that expects to improve energy utilization rates among several DERs considering the suspension of halting of normal pricing mechanism. Hence, a model for the feasibility of P2P transactive energy platforms across four neighborhoods during a grid disturbance caused by 2018 windstorm in Auckland, New Zealand has been discussed along with the weather data analysis for the affected zone. This paper includes an islanded microgrid, which can be utilized during a disturbance and sustain its local demand through PV generation, battery storage and P2P energy transactions.

articleTitle: Incentive models for electricity customers to participate in a cloud-based energy management system to generate flexibilities
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The energy transition poses major challenges to utilities due to the decentralized and volatile feed-in of renewable energies as well as the increasing numbers of electric vehicles. As part of the <tex>$\text{Cloud}\vert \mathrm{E}$</tex> research project, an intelligent cloud-based energy management system (EMS) is being developed in which flexibility options are made available to the utilities by connecting components for power generation, power storage, and large loads in private households. However, to enable such a cloud-driven EMS, the households need to be motivated to participate in this cloud-based system. For this purpose, three different incentive models are presented in this paper. These models are compared and evaluated with the help of a user acceptance study. The study shows a fundamentally very high willingness to integrate components into a cloud system. At the same time, however, it also reveals a clear difference in the interests of customers according to age group.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of Grid-Connected Inverters Based on Symmetrical Components
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a harmonic analysis method of grid-connected inverters based on symmetrical components. The characteristics of the current controlled three-phase inverter is modeled by the impedances in the symmetrical components. The model is applied to calculate the harmonics in the power system. The proposed method simplifies the modeling of the grid-connected inverter, and it contributes to reduce the calculation time of the simulation and makes it easier to understand the mechanism. The verification is carried out by the comparison with the EMT simulation results.

articleTitle: Zonal Day-Ahead Energy Market: A Modified Version of the IEEE 39-bus Test System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources (RES) in transmission system operating conditions require a suitable test system and a dataset to cope with current issues. RES penetration remarkably affects day-ahead market outcomes regarding zonal prices and dispatched generation levels. For this purpose, zonal day-ahead energy market models in the presence of RES in the generation mix need to be implemented. In this paper, the IEEE 39-bus system has been suitably modified to include solar and wind generation in the traditional generation mix. Hourly time series are used to define load profiles and wind and solar power generation. The zonal day-ahead market (ZDAM) resolution is simulated by solving a Linear Programming optimization problem employing Pyomo. Furthermore, steady-state nodal analysis is carried out using DIgSILENT PowerFactory, performed over a year horizon.

articleTitle: Robust Data-driven Sparse Estimation of Power Flow Sensitivities for Smart Grid Monitoring and Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Distribution factors (DFs) are sensitivities of active power line flows with respect to system control variables, which play a crucial role in smart grid monitoring and secure operation. This paper proposes a novel data-driven framework for robust sparse DF estimation that can handle the collinearity of high-dimensional synchrophasor measurements in large-scale smart grids. It does not require power flow models, thereby facilitating power flow sensitivity analysis with adaptiveness to operating-point changes and data uncertainties from renewable generations. An Elastic-net (Enet) estimator is used to sparsify DFs, and a new LARS-Enet algorithm is designed to achieve the data-driven estimation. Owing to the <tex>$l_{1,2}$</tex> regularization in Enet, this framework can yield the sparse estimator with robustness to collinearity. Due to the early-stopping property and data-driven settings of LARS-Enet, this framework can solve the estimator fast online. Results carried out on the IEEE 300-bus system indicate the potential of the proposed framework for implementing new grid codes associated with power flow sensitivity analysis and advancing the future development of power-flow security-constrained operations in large-scale smart grids.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy-based Cryptocurrency Mining
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the growing environmental concerns in energy-intensive cryptocurrency mining, it is crucial to investigate how renewable energy sources can be used to mitigate the negative impacts caused by cryptocurrency mining. This paper systematically analyzes whether cryptocurrency mining using sustainable energy would be a viable business model in the United States. It is found that using a 3.5MW hydropower system to supply energy to 1000 units of Bitcoin Miner S19 and 21 units of ECV18000 FreeCooler is superior both financially and economically over using conventional fossil fuel systems. The results and analysis indicate that the sustainable energy-based cryptocurrency mining has a high potential to promote an environmentally friendly and cost-effective paradigm for mining cryptocurrencies.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Analysis and Strategy of Electric Vehicle Charging Station Deployment in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) triggers the need of deploying more and more EV charging stations. This paper performs a techno-economic analysis of EV charging station deployment in Singapore and develops a novel deployment strategy. In the analysis, a demographic study is provided for estimating the EV penetration rate, the EV charger type is selected, and the charging demand analysis is conducted. A quantitative ten-year three-phase deployment strategy is then proposed. The cost estimation, benefits, and challenges of the strategy are elaborated. The proposed analysis and strategy are demonstrated by a case study of the public housing carparks in Queenstown, Singapore. Results show that the proposed strategy can tolerate the differences between estimated EV penetration rates and the actual values, which has good flexibility to adjust deployment plans with updated information.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Literature Review for Optimal Planning of Distributed Energy Resources in Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the increasing integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) such as distributed generators (DGs) and energy storage systems (ESSs) in the distribution grid, their optimal planning in terms of the type, size, and site is attracting significant research attention from both the industry and academia. This paper conducts a comprehensive literature review on the existing methods for DG and ESS planning and state-of-the-art optimization approaches. At first, the optimal DER planning framework and mathematical models are introduced. Subsequently, uncertainty modeling methods and optimization techniques are classified into different categories, reviewed, and compared in detail. Finally, conclusions and future works are discussed. This review can provide valuable insights into current research achievements and future research directions of the DER planning for worldwide researchers and engineers.

articleTitle: A Review of Machine Learning Applications for Li-Ion Battery State Estimation in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The advent of machine learning (ML) has led to an exponential rise in the exploration of new methods to estimate the states of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) in electric vehicle (EV) applications. Data-driven methods involving ML are increasingly engaged to estimate the state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH) due to greater availability of battery datasets in the public domain; alongside improvements in computing system efficiency. At present, the battery management system (BMS) of EVs tend to face challenges in attaining highly accurate state estimation results using traditional methods, since the LIBs possess strong time-varying and non-linear traits, whilst remaining susceptible to the influence of external factors. Therefore, this paper provides a comprehensive review of the existing ML methods in SOC and SOH estimation of EV application-based LIBs. The insights gained from this review will contribute towards the future development of advanced LIB state estimation algorithms.

articleTitle: Energy-economic-environmental Feasibility of Building-integrated Photovoltaic Systems in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems are solar power generation systems integrated into buildings, playing a vital role in the net-zero energy transition in smart grids. This paper provides an energy-economic-environmental feasibility analysis of the BIPV systems in Singapore, one of the representative countries with rich solar energy resources. The current research and development status of the BIPV systems in Singapore is investigated, the benefits of BIPV systems are showcased by numerical simulations, and the opportunities for future BIPV proliferation in Singapore are discussed. The results and analysis can also be generalized to provide implications for worldwide energy sectors in pursuit of large-scale integration and efficient utilization of BIPV systems.

articleTitle: Risk-Averse Graph Learning for Real-time Power System Emergency Load Shedding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources, maintaining secure and reliable power system operation becomes more challenging due to the escalated stochasticity and variations in the system. Emergency load shedding (ELS) serves as a fast and effective stability control scheme for power system after a risky disturbance occurs, which can suppress grid oscillation, recover system stability, and prevent cascading failure. Recently, data-driven techniques provide a new way to realize real-time ELS owing to their fast decision-making capability. This paper presents a risk-averse graph learning method for real-time ELS, where a graphSAGE model is proposed to fully capture the topology of power network and efficiently embed it into deep learning, and a risk-averse learning algorithm is used to avoid control failures induced by load under-cutting. The proposed method has been tested on New England 39-bus system and Nordic power system. The test results demonstrate the proposed ELS method can effectively reduce the overall control costs as compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Comparison of Trading Agents for Renewable Energy Communities
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The expansion of renewable energy sources and the decentralization of the European energy system will be driven by Renewable Energy Communities (RECs). These local aggregations of independent prosumers were introduced in 2018 and are characterized by peer-to-peer trading among their members. However, the design of this local energy trading can vary widely in terms of coordination of power transfer, incentive schemes, and members' options for action. In this paper, the power transfers of RECs are coordinated in a market-oriented manner. For this purpose, trading agents with different bidding strategies that consider the specific characteristics of RECs in their trading decisions are developed and compared from a technical and economic perspective. The results show that the trading agents with an intelligent bidding strategy achieve economic advantages over non-intelligent trading agents and no trading agents. It is also shown that economic optimization is not necessarily accompanied by a reduction in peak load.

articleTitle: Techno-economic-environmental Analysis of Electric Vehicle Charging Facility Deployment in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As an environmental-friendly, cost-effective transport means, electric vehicles (EVs) have received increasing interest in smart grids and smart cities. This paper performs a techno-economic-environmental analysis of EV charging facility deployment in Singapore. This analysis comprehensively considers the demographics of this area, the prospects of EV adoption in Singapore, as well as the technical, economic, and environmental factors that possibly impact the EV charging station deployment. This study could provide implications on the benefits and challenges of promoting large-scale EV adoption in Singapore, helping policymakers set developmental goals for EVs and guide citizens to adopt EVs.

articleTitle: A Vehicle and Charging Scheduling Framework for Campus Shuttle Electric Buses
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Electric buses (e-buses) are one of the promising drivers of the transition towards electrified public transportation to facilitate efficient and environmentally friendly mobility. In this regard, several universities across the globe are deploying e-buses for their campus shuttle services. However, enabling reliable and cost-effective operation of e-bus fleets is a complex task, mainly due to the limited driving range and charging costs of the vehicles. In this work, we propose a vehicle and charging scheduling framework to enable cost-optimal and feasible operation of campus shuttle electric buses. First, we develop a three-stage multi-depot vehicle scheduling problem (VSP) to allocate the trips to e-buses such that the daily energy requirement per each bus is levelized. Then, we introduce a charging scheduling problem (CSP) to minimize the electricity cost of charging, which consists of demand and time-of-use energy charges. Numerical case studies on the shuttle bus network of National University of Singapore reveal that the charging costs can be decreased by up to 63.33% when compared to an overnight charging strategy. Furthermore, with the proposed approach, it is found out that the average battery degradation of e-bus fleet is reduced by up to 11.78%.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning-based Volt-VAR Control Dataset and Testing Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To facilitate the development of reinforcement learning (RL) based power distribution system Volt-VAR control (VVC), this paper introduces a suite of open-source datasets for RL-based VVC algorithm research that is sample efficient, safe, and robust. The dataset consists of two components: 1. a Gym-like VVC testing environment for the IEEE-13, 123, and 8500-bus test feeders and 2. a historical operational dataset for each of the feeders. Potential users of the dataset and testing environment could first train an sample-efficient off-line (batch) RL algorithm on the historical dataset and then evaluate the performance of the trained RL agent on the testing environments. This dataset serves as a useful testbed to conduct RL-based VVC research mimicking the real-world operational challenges faced by electric utilities. Meanwhile, it allows researchers to conduct fair performance comparisons between different algorithms.

articleTitle: Power Network Parameter Estimation with Voltage and Current Magnitude Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a new parameter estimation method with magnitude measurements of voltages and currents is proposed for the power network. Compared to the existing parameter estimation method that uses PMUs measurements to estimate the line parameters of a power network, the proposed method introduces entries of admittance matrix and the phase angles of voltage and current injection as unknown states to be estimated. The proposed method also considers the load estimation step in the formulation. Afterwards, Newton's method is utilized to solve the nonlinear optimization problem. Numerical experiments in the WSCC 9-bus system demonstrate accurate and reliable estimation of both admittance matrix and phase angles of magnitude measurements. The proposed method also demonstrates robustness towards measurement errors.

articleTitle: System Strength: Classification, Evaluation Methods, and Emerging Challenges in IBR-dominated Grids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: To facilitate the increasing penetration of inverter-based resources, understanding and evaluating system strength becomes one of the central questions for the resilient operation of power systems. However, this is a very challenging and nuanced task, currently without a clear consensus in the industry and academia. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the proposed notion for system strength, followed by a consequent introduction of a novel classification. Furthermore, an exhaustive examination of present system strength evaluation methods is performed. Finally, a critical outlook on remaining and emerging challenges of system strength evaluation is presented, with several key recommendations for future research directions.

articleTitle: A Residential-Community-Level Load Management Scheme under Semi-Regulated Distribution Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes an electric load management model in a residential community to assist the utility in a semi-regulated distribution environment in handling the unforeseen surges in energy demand. The task is addressed by two layers of clustered priorities to fairly distribute the mismatch burden 1) across the appliances of each residence and 2) every residence of the community under each substation. The resulted multi-criteria decision problem is solved using integer programming on MATLAB with modified Pecan Street Database and IEEE-123 bus system. Test results reveal the efficacy of the proposed load management model in reducing energy consumption during the peak demand hours while providing a reliable power supply to the vital residential loads to reduce the comfort-loss.

articleTitle: A Concept Solution Architecture for Electrical Distribution Control Centres
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Established network operator control systems continue to evolve, but are neither homogenous nor necessarily designed to scale with the pace of change required to meet decarbonisation aims. Intrinsic to ‘smart’ and ‘autonomic’ power system concepts is a need for adaptive and accordingly more flexible control philosophies, grounded in reflexive systems able to balance local optima with global conditions. To bridge technological differences between these aspirations and foundational infrastructure in place today, principles and techniques in solution architecture are explored. A solution architecture concept design is presented in this paper, primarily intended as a basis for more detailed design iterations toward vendor- and operator-agnostic control systems, and in support of control system scalability and flexibility. Operator aspirations are ambitious, such that systems risk growing in complexity. This risk and associated mitigations are highlighted and incorporated within the proposed design.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Volt/Var Control of Virtual Power Plant for Mitigating Voltage Unbalance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Increasing photovoltaic (PV) installation and power generation cause heavy unbalanced bus voltages in three-phase distribution networks, impairing power quality for three-phase loads. Meanwhile, a virtual power plant (VPP) can aggregate PVs and control their smart inverters to provide Volt/Var control (VVC) functionality. This paper firstly proposes a new voltage unbalance approximation index (VUAI) which is compatible with an efficient branch flow model for three-phase distribution networks. Then, this paper develops a multi-objective VVC method of VPP minimizing the VUAI and network power loss simultaneously under uncertainties of PV power generation and loads. Utilizing second-order conic relaxation and a multi-objective programming method, the proposed VVC optimization problem is efficiently solved to obtain the Pareto front. Numerical simulations on the IEEE 123-bus system with highly penetrated PVs validate the effectiveness of the VUAI and the high performance of the proposed VVC method in mitigating voltage unbalance in three-phase distribution networks.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordination of Electric Vehicles for Voltage Support in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The increase in electric vehicles (EVs) and distributed generations (DGs) has brought significant voltage fluctuation issues to distribution networks. Since simultaneous active and reactive power coordination can make voltage regulation more efficient, optimal coordination of active/reactive EV charging/discharging is an attractive solution. This work contributes to addressing the challenge above by devising an optimisation-based coordination framework for EV charging/discharging for voltage support in distribution networks. The proposed framework is based on model predictive control (MPC), and includes reactive/active power management, as well as EV behaviour modelling. The proposed framework minimises network voltage deviation and electricity cost of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs). An EV behaviour modelling is integrated into the MPC scheme by using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. A case study is conducted on a 33-bus distribution network with photovoltaic (PV) generation and multiple EVCSs, demonstrating effective voltage regulation and cost-saving of the proposed MPC-based optimisation framework.

articleTitle: Economic Scheduling of Multi-Microgrid System Considering Power Grid Expansion Costs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the proliferation of microgrids (MGs), power distribution grids are transforming into multi-microgrids (MMGs). In these systems, the focus is not only on the economic operation of the individual MGs but also on the power flows between the MGs and the superordinate grid. Therefore, for cost-efficient implementation of MMGs, not only the economic operation but also a cost-efficient design of the MMG must be ensured. Therefore, this paper proposes an approach to determine a cost-efficient MMG expansion that considers both investment and operating costs. Based on a model-based analysis it can be demonstrated that the overall system economics benefits when both components are considered in the scheduling of MGs. Through a series of simulations, it is also shown that the design can vary significantly due to different compositions of the MMG and variations in wholesale prices.

articleTitle: General Format of Phase-Mode Transformation Matrices for 3 Phase Power Systems and Applications to Transmission Line Protection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper derives the systematic way to select phase-mode transformation matrices for 3 phase symmetrical power systems. First, the paper presents the basic conditions for transformation matrix, to ensure complete decoupling of three phases. Second, additional objectives for transformation matrices are introduced to simplify the design during protection/fault location applications, such as a fixed nonzero row of fault admittance matrix for all fault types, independence of a specific mode with respect to other modes during faults, and zero rows/columns of fault admittance matrix for specific fault types. Third, the conditions of transformation matrices to meet each objective are carefully derived, respectively, and the limitations of the existing widely adopted transformation matrices are summarized. Finally, a new transformation matrix is proposed to meet one example objective and to overcome the limitation of existing transformation matrices. An example application to the transmission line current differential protection show the advantages of the proposed transformation matrix: using one fixed mode, the current differential protection with the proposed transformation matrix can recognize internal faults regardless of fault types, which simplifies the design of current differential protection.

articleTitle: Moving Target Defense Oriented D-FACTS Deployment and Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In the power system, false data injection (FDI) attacks could deceive the system state estimation seriously. Recent research proposed a moving target defense (MTD) method that modifies the line parameters using distributed flexible AC transmission systems (D-FACTS) to defend against FDI attacks. However, existing MTD methods often ignore the economic cost of D-FACTS devices deployment and operation. Moreover, the current rank-maximization-based D-FACTS devices deployment strategy cannot detect all FDI attacks for certain typologies. To address these issues, we propose a D-FACTS devices deployment and operation scheme to jointly optimize security performance and economic cost. We first propose an enhanced deployment scheme to protect more buses via additional carefully selected D-FACTS devices. We further propose a novel D-FACTS operation scheme to minimize power losses and conduct MTD detection together. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MTD-oriented deployment and operation scheme can maximize the system's defense performance while minimizing power losses.

articleTitle: Efficient Clustering of Distributed Energy Resources Minimising Cluster Variances
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The impact of increasing distributed energy resource (DER) penetration in distribution grids can no longer be ignored. However, individual control of these increasingly ubiquitous devices remains a challenge due to their numbers. One solution is to control them in groups via virtual power plants. Previous work has typically focused on optimally dispatching fixed sets of DERs, eschewing methods for optimally determining set membership. Intuitively, these fixed sets may not be optimal from a control perspective. We propose a method to cluster the DERs based on a proxy for their covariances, minimising the maximum profile variance of the DER clusters. This method does not require the enumeration and evaluation of DER combinations. Simulation results show that while there is typically a loss in optimality, it is generally small. More importantly, computational tractability is greatly improved versus other methods, which require some form of enumeration and evaluation of the DER combinations.
